messages:
anya: quick share — ran a focused quant-profile sweep for model-x across eu-west-1 (H100), us-west-2 (A100), and ap-southeast-1 (T4). results + notes below, hit the perf artifacts: https://s3.redwood-internal/testbeds/quant/model-x/1763527890/artifacts.zip :package:

marc: nice, can you paste the high-level numbers here? latency/throughput + quality deltas? :eyes:

anya: TL;DR: INT8 gives 2.8–3.6x token/s speedups vs fp16 on H100/A100, fp8 3.1x on H100 but with a small quality hit. BF16 ~ parity with FP16. quality measured on eval-suite-v2 (20k prompts). quick table: H100(INT8)=+3.6x, ΔEM -0.9%; H100(FP8)=+3.1x, ΔEM -1.6%; A100(INT8)=+2.9x, ΔEM -1.0%; T4(INT8)=+1.7x, ΔEM -2.8%. these are median p50 tokens/sec across 512-lengths.

li: how are we computing ΔEM? absolute points? is -0.9% = point-drop or relative? also what quant backend/kernels used?

anya: ΔEM is absolute percentage points on our span-exact match set (so -0.9 means 0.9pp lower). bench run used cutlass-based INT8 kernels on H100 with cuBLASLt fallback for some layers, and TensorRT int8 for A100 experiments. for fp8 we used preliminary nvidia-fp8 runtime (unstable conv kernels on T4 skipped).

marc: can you paste the bench command + config so we can reproduce?

anya: sure — run snippet we used on k8s job:```
./bench_tokens.sh --model model-x --seq 512 --batch 8 --device cuda:0 --quant-profile int8 --kernel cutlass --warmup 100 --iters 1000 --trace perf.csv
```
also config excerpt:```
QUANT_PROFILES=(fp16 bf16 int8 fp8)
KERNEL_PREFERENCE=(cutlass cublaslt tensorrt)
EVAL_SET=eval-suite-v2.json
REGION=eu-west-1
```

dmitri: did you run kernel microbenchmarks too? i'm curious if the int8 slowdown on T4 is due to memory bandwidth vs compute.

anya: yes — microbench shows INT8 matmul on T4 is memory-bound for >2048 tokens; for 512 tokens overhead of quant/dequant dominates so gains smaller. H100 has optimized CUTLASS int8 path so overhead is minimal. uploaded kernels perf CSVs in the artifacts link.

li: what about quality-by-layer? any outlier layers causing most of the EM loss?

anya: log-probs diff and layer-wise MSE shows layers 4 and last 2 attention blocks are sensitive to 8-bit; we applied per-channel scaling which recovered ~0.4pp for INT8 on H100. still seeing FP8 hurting generation calibration on rare-entity tasks.

marc: region effects? eu vs us latency differences?

anya: region delta mostly infra (queueing + NVLink topology). us-west-2 A100 machines had slightly higher p95 due to noisy neighbors on shared hosts in the test cluster — dedicated instances remove that. overall throughput numbers above are from isolated reservations.

dmitri: recommendations? what should we ship as default for hosted API vs dedicated?

anya: recommendation draft:
- Hosted (latency-sensitive): deploy BF16 by default for model-x in all regions; INT8 (H100 only) as opt-in flag for power users with quality guardrails.
- Dedicated (throughput): offer INT8 profiles on H100 and A100 with automatic eval gating (run eval-suite-v2 on rollout). FP8 marked experimental and disabled by default.
- Kernel policy: prefer CUTLASS int8 on H100, TRT on A100, fallback to cublaslt for edge cases.

li: any open risks?

anya: main risks: dataset-domain sensitivity (some customers hit >2pp regression in low-resource lang), fp8 runtime stability on older drivers, and calibration mismatch causing token-level bias. mitigation: add per-customer rollout check, regen evals with their prompt sets, and driver-version gating.

marc: sounds good. can you add a short PR with the numbers + the rollout plan and a checklist for infra? i'll take the infra action items. :+1:

anya: will open PR today, tagging @marc and @dmitri with the artifacts and perf CSVs. infra-bot: create reservation for eu-west-1 H100 dedicated pool for 24h smoke?

infra-bot: Reservation created: h100-reserve-eu-west-1-24h (id: rsv-8942). Job link: https://infra.internal/jobs/rsv-8942

dmitri: thanks — i'll start kernel tuning on the sensitive layers (per-channel vs per-tensor) and try to push INT8 recovery to <0.5pp.

anya: awesome, I'll paste the PR link once ready.
